options.pitch: ElevenLabs, the AI voice company used by creators and dubbing studios, agreed to buy Japanese voice firm Kotoba for a reported $100 million, three months after a sale valued it at $22 billion. The biggest AI voice company just paid about $100 million to buy Japanese speech instead of building it, so voice actors, dubbers and audiobook narrators can see what one language is worth to the firms cloning voices.
options.why_now: Music Business Worldwide, 16 Nov 2026, reporting Business Insider Japan.

options.pitch: Kling, the AI video tool sold to filmmakers and creators, raised 19.8 billion yuan in October, and its owner's accounts book a yearly return on a promise to buy those investors out. The money behind a famous AI video tool used by filmmakers and creators is partly a loan in disguise: its backers can ask for their money back with interest, so anyone choosing which AI video tool to build on can see how safe its funding really is.

Sonilo, an $11 million AI music start-up, will pay licence fees and a share of revenue to Symphonic's independent artists who opt in to train its model, and the rate is private. Independent musicians can now be paid to have an AI learn from their songs, through their distributor, but only if they tick the box, and nobody has said the rate: anyone with music on a distributor knows which email to read.

iQIYI released 21 AI-generated short dramas in one quarter and took first place in China's short-drama market, in the same results where its revenue fell 10% to RMB6.01 billion. Chinese streamer iQIYI pays the studios that make its short dramas a share of what viewers watch instead of a fixed fee, so any producer selling drama to a streamer knows who now carries the cost of making it.
options.why_now: iQIYI third-quarter 2026 results and earnings call, 16 Nov 2026.
